newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BAT puts bought ahead of ex-dividend.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BAT puts bought ahead of ex-dividend.

text.p: Traded options in tobacco-to-insurance group BAT Industries were busy on Friday, owing to an arbitrage opportunity ahead of the shares going ex-dividend on Monday, dealers said.

The chief deal was the purchase of deep in-the-money puts -- which have a large amount of time value premium -- against buying stock. In this way a profit can be locked in by collecting the dividend and then exercising the puts.
A large number of options need to be bought because of the small amount of profit per share that can be made.
The actual deal was for the purchase of 10,000 April 800 puts in BAT at 286p as well as 10 million of the underlying shares at 535p each. This makes a net debit of 821p per share.
On Monday, the shares will go ex-dividend by 20p gross -- which includes a Foreign Income Dividend (FID) of 17.5p, which does not attract tax.

From Monday, the options can be exercised to sell 10 million shares at 800p. After adding the 20p dividend amount, the net credit will be 820p which makes an overall risk-free profit of 1p per share, or 100,000 stg for the size of this deal.
By 1317 GMT, BAT shares were down 26-1/2p to 528p.
Elsewhere a call spread was established in pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome, in which 650 April 1000 calls were sold at 120p and 650 April 1050 calls bought at 70p for a net credit of 50p.

The underlying shares need to fall below 1000p by April expiry in order to collect the maximum 50p profit. These shares will also go ex-dividend on Monday by about 22.56p gross -- a figure which includes an FID of 4.75p.
